key_insight: CGMap uses distance-resolved graph learning to turn scattered cancer-related signals into an interpretable ranking of candidate genes. This helps researchers narrow the search space and connect computational hypotheses to practical validation.
problem_solved: Cancer-related signals can be dispersed across biological networks, making it difficult to identify which genes deserve follow-up and understand why they were prioritized.
method: Use a distance-resolved graph-learning framework to organize dispersed oncogenic signals.
Map those signals into structured priorities for candidate cancer genes.
Provide an interpretable path from gene-prioritization hypotheses to practical validation.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, CGMap illustrates how graph learning can support interpretable prioritization in biomedical research. Its focus on narrowing candidate sets connects model outputs to actionable experimental follow-up.
visual_elements: Biological network diagram with cancer-related signals highlighted at different graph distances.
Workflow: dispersed signals → CGMap → ranked genes → validation.
Candidate-selection funnel showing a broad gene pool narrowed to priority targets.
Illustrative ranked-gene panel with visual links to supporting network signals.
paper_title: Interpretable distance-resolved graph learning for cancer gene priority screening
paper_authors: Chenhao Wang, Shidong Xu, Li Tang, Gang Luo, Yongchang Zhang
